newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: W&H board to meet Wednesday on bid.
newsitem.headline: W&H board to meet Wednesday on bid.

text.p: The board of New Zealand publisher Wilson and Horton Ltd will meet on Wednesday to discuss a full takeover bid by Ireland's Independent Newspapers Plc, Managing Director John Maasland said on Tuesday.
Maasland said the board would discuss the commissioning of an independent appraisal report on the NZ$10.50/share bid.

"We may not have selected that appraiser by then (Wednesday), we may in fact have a number of people we wish to talk to to seek their capability so far as the Stock Exchange is concerned," Maasland said.
The NZSE must approve the independence of the appraiser.
Maasland said the report would need to be done by the time of Independent's stand in the market for Wilson and Horton shares, expected around October 8.
Independent is also making a written offer, allowing shareholders to opt for cash or take part of their entitlement in Independent exchangeable preference shares.
Initial market reaction on Tuesday was that the price was too low, with Wilson and Horton gaining $1.00 to $10.70 on low volume. Maasland declined to comment.
The company has advised shareholders not to sell pending the independent appraisal.
Independent Newspapers Plc already holds 22.6 percent of Wilson and Horton, with the same amount held by family trusts linked to Independent's biggest shareholder Tony O'Reilly.
